title: Do Verifiers Reduce Security-Relevant Misconfigurations? A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Verifier-in-the-Loop GVR for Intent-to-Configuration
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment to test whether embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces security-increasing (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations produced by an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline. Under a frozen protocol (preregistration cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1) we used Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation, two deterministic validators combined by logical OR, and a shared_initial_candidate generation contract to conserve model calls. We ran N = 300 matched intents (150 benign + 150 programmatic adversarial variants) with a declared model gpt-5-mini. Execution completed all planned episodes with model_calls_used = 300 and no failures. Confirmatory outcome: baseline_success = 300 and guarded_success = 300 (contingency n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0); no validator reported forbidden reachability and no repair calls were invoked. Paired risk-difference = 0.0, McNemar two-sided p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Because the repair path was never exercised, the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis about repair efficacy is untestable in this run; the primary empirical contribution is deterministic execution accounting, a tight descriptive upper bound on baseline violation rate (one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound ≈ 0.00994), and artifact-grounded operational design lessons to guide follow-up stress tests that intentionally exercise repair. All preregistration, per-episode validator traces, provider audits, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device configuration, but misconfigurations that expand attack surface or violate access-control policies are a critical operational risk. Prior system and survey work therefore recommends execution oracles, constrained generation, and iterative generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures as mitigations.

Research question and scope. We asked a focused operational question, preregistered before execution, and executed a deterministic paired experiment: Does embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a GVR loop reduce the incidence of forbidden-reachability misconfigurations produced by an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline when exposed to adversarially perturbed intents?

Summary of what we did. We preregistered study cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1, implemented a Dockerized deterministic emulator with two validators (a containerized Batfish-style execution validator and a lightweight Python graph-based static reachability analyzer), and ran a matched-pair design on N = 300 paired intents. To limit model-call costs under the adapter contract we used shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single LLM generation per pair was replayed to both arms (baseline and guarded). The guarded arm would invoke at most one repair LLM call if any validator detected forbidden reachability.

Principal outcome and interpretation. All 300 paired intents passed the forbidden-reachability predicate in both arms (n11 = 300); validators never reported forbidden reachability and the repair step was never invoked. Because no discordant pairs occurred, the preregistered confirmatory test of repair efficacy is untestable under the observed data and the chosen generation semantics. The run nevertheless provides precise deterministic accounting (model_calls_used = 300, planned episodes = 600, completed = 600, failed = 0), artifact-backed numerical bounds on undetected baseline violation rates (one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound ≈ 0.00994), and concrete design lessons for follow-up stress tests intended to exercise the repair path.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, deterministic, paired execution and full artifact archive that documents provider accounting and per-episode validator traces; (2) a concise, artifact-grounded null result that bounds baseline violation rates and shows that, under shared replay semantics and the chosen adversary/verifier/model, verifier insertion did not change observed compliance; (3) explicit design recommendations (generation semantics, adversary potency, repair budget, verifier diversity) grounded in the archived execution manifest and analysis outputs; (4) reproducibility artifacts supporting deterministic replay and targeted follow-up experiments.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and execution-guided repair. Recent system papers and experimental work demonstrate that verifier or execution feedback can materially improve correctness of generated code and Infrastructure-as-Code when the verifier detects errors and repair strategies are effective; however, realized gains depend on verifier strength and repair design [TerraFormer et al., doi:10.1145/3786583.3786898].

LLMs for intent-driven NetOps. Surveys and applied NetOps work report both promise and risks—LLM hallucination, overconfidence, and domain mismatch—and argue for validators, constrained templates, or human oversight for operational safety [comprehensive surveys, e.g., https://openalex.org/W4415071524; Intent-LLM system descriptions].

Execution-based validation and testbeds. Emulation and testbed studies show execution-based validators and deterministic emulation permit reproducible evaluation of generated configurations but warn about external-validity gaps to production devices or live traffic [Dockerized FRR-style emulation and testbed descriptions].

Gap and positioning. The literature motivates verifier-in-the-loop architectures but contains limited preregistered, deterministic paired evaluations that (a) fix generation semantics explicitly, (b) archive per-episode verifier traces and provider audits for deterministic accounting, and (c) quantify how design choices (shared vs independent generation, repair budget, adversary strength) determine whether the repair path will be exercised. Our study fills that niche by delivering a fully archived paired run and by reporting the degenerate, artifact-verified outcome together with practical design guidance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1) fixed a paired-binary confirmatory design with N = 300 matched intents (150 benign seeds and one programmatic adversarial variant per seed). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in proportion of intents yielding forbidden reachability). The preregistration specified an exact McNemar two-sided test (alpha = 0.05) and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs; final analysis used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (this bootstrap parameter and seed are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Generation contract and adapter constraints. To conserve provider usage the adapter was executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics: one initial LLM candidate was generated per pair and the same candidate replayed to both arms. This contract produces one hosted-model generation per paired intent (model_calls_used = 300 for 300 pairs) and is recorded in the provider-call audit (execution/execution_manifest.json). The contract was preregistered and is central to interpreting inferential power because replay reduces between-arm sampling variance.

Definition of the forbidden-reachability predicate and validators (concise technical statement). Forbidden reachability is a binary predicate evaluated on the emulator's post-change network state: given a set of policy constraints and protected source–destination pairs encoded in the task payload, forbidden_reachability = true if the final configuration enables reachability from any source to any destination that the task's policy or protected set marks as disallowed. The exact source/destination groups for each intent are deterministic parts of the archived task payloads (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Two deterministic validators assessed this predicate per episode: (1) a containerized Batfish-style execution validator that applies the generated configuration to a deterministic FRRouting-style topology and executes reachability/route-policy checks using the emulator's forwarding semantics; (2) a lightweight Python graph-based static reachability analyzer that computes reachability on a parsed network-state graph. The scoring decision rule is a logical OR: a pair is labeled 'violating' if any validator reports forbidden reachability. Per-episode validator outputs and their 'violation_count' fields are archived in execution/scoring/*.json.

Intervention arms and repair policy. Baseline = replay of the shared initial candidate. Guarded = the same replayed candidate validated by the two validators; if any validator reports forbidden_reachability the preregistered repair policy allowed up to one repair LLM call to attempt a corrected configuration. Repair attempts are logged per episode; across the run no repair prompt was issued because validators never flagged forbidden reachability.

Execution, determinism, and artifacts. The environment used Dockerized FRRouting-style images and deterministic orchestration; seeds, task payloads, provider-call traces, and per-episode validator_trace objects are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/execution_manifest.json). The manifest records planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 300, and the model configuration declaring 'gpt-5-mini' (execution/model_configuration.json).

Analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided test on complete matched pairs; prespecified 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (final: 10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Sensitivity analyses prespecified in the preregistration treat technical/model failures as violations; because no technical failures occurred these sensitivity analyses coincide with the primary analysis. All per-episode outcomes, provider audits, and validator traces were recorded for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The deterministic run completed planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions) with completed = 600 and failed episodes = 0. Provider-call accounting under shared_initial_candidate shows model_calls_used = 300 (execution/execution_manifest.json; execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = 'gpt-5-mini' and requested_model = 'gpt-5-mini'). The provider-call audit stage_counts show 'shared_initial_generation' = 300.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The paired contingency from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (Table 1). Baseline_success_count = 300 and guarded_success_count = 300. The paired risk-difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The prespecified bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) for the paired risk-difference is [0.0, 0.0] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg).

Descriptive bound on undetected baseline violation rate. Observing 0 violations in N = 300 independent episodes produces a one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound on the baseline violation probability of 1 - 0.05^(1/300) ≈ 0.00994 (≈0.994%). We report this numeric bound as a descriptive constraint on undetected baseline violations under the chosen model, validators, emulator, and task set; the bound follows directly from the archived per-episode success counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair activity and verifier concordance. Because validators never reported forbidden reachability on any initial candidate, no repair call was invoked and all per-episode validator_trace.repair_applied flags are false. Per-episode traces record validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true in every archived scoring artifact (execution/scoring/*.json). Verifier_disagreement_rate across the two validators is 0 in the archived analysis artifacts.

Representative examples. Representative per-task artifacts (execution/responses/task-000001-*.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json) illustrate typical medium- and hard-pattern transitions where the shared candidate matched the reference answer and validator traces report no violations. These representative artifacts are archived for deterministic spot-checking of parsing, normalization, and validator judgments.
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory test is uninformative here. The paired McNemar test compares discordant outcomes (n10 and n01); with n10 = n01 = 0 there are no discordant pairs to compare and the test is therefore uninformative about repair efficacy. Two coupled design facts recorded in the artifacts produced this degenerate contingency: (1) the shared_initial_candidate contract deliberately reduced between-arm sampling variance by replaying a single LLM candidate to both arms (provider-call audit: shared_initial_generation = 300), and (2) for the chosen model, validators, emulator, and programmatic adversarial perturbations, no initial candidate triggered the forbidden-reachability predicate. Consequently, the experiment can only bound baseline violation probability under these exact conditions rather than show that verifier-guided repair can rescue violations.

Design lessons (artifact-grounded). 1) Generation semantics matter: shared replay reduces model-call cost (model_calls_used = 300 vs up to 600) but also reduces independent-sample variability required to produce discordant violating outputs; for experiments explicitly intended to evaluate repair efficacy use independent-condition generation (two LLM draws per pair) or increase repair-call budgets. 2) Adversary potency matters: the programmatic adversarial variants archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl did not trigger validator-detectable forbidden reachability for this model/validator pair; targeted adversary generation or stronger perturbations are necessary to exercise repairs. 3) Verifier strength and diversity matter: we used two deterministic validators combined by logical OR; broader oracle families or production-grade execution oracles may detect violations missed here. 4) Reproducible accounting is feasible: the run archives provider-call audits, per-episode validator traces, and deterministic task manifests enabling exact replay of the observed accounting and contingency.

Threats to validity (artifact pointers). Internal validity: reduced by shared_initial_candidate semantics and single-model scope (execution/model_configuration.json; deterministic_reconciliation.json). Construct validity: whether the forbidden-reachability predicate and the two validators adequately model operational security risk depends on task payloads and validator algorithms; validator IDs and versions are recorded per episode (execution/scoring/*.json) for independent assessment. External validity: tasks were synthetic and executed in Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation and may not generalize to heterogeneous production devices or live traffic (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Conclusion validity: the observed contingency is degenerate and the preregistered power assumptions (expected nonzero baseline violation rate) are not met. All of these threats are enumerated in the archived limitations and execution manifest to permit transparent reanalysis.

Practical implications. Under the exact contract and artifact conditions here, inserting a verifier did not change observed compliance because baseline configurations already satisfied the safety predicate; this should not be interpreted as evidence that verifiers are unnecessary in general. Instead, our artifact-backed conclusion is operationally narrow and actionable: for a study to demonstrate repair efficacy researchers must choose generation semantics, adversarial examples, repair budgets, and verifier families that together create opportunities for repair to be invoked and evaluated.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a deterministic paired evaluation of a verifier-in-the-loop GVR pipeline for intent→configuration with declared model gpt-5-mini, two deterministic validators combined by logical OR, and shared_initial_candidate generation semantics. The run completed N = 300 matched pairs and produced a degenerate contingency: both baseline and guarded arms passed the forbidden-reachability predicate on all pairs (n11 = 300). Because no validator ever reported forbidden reachability the repair path was never exercised and the confirmatory hypothesis about repair efficacy is untestable under the observed data and chosen contract. The run yields a tight descriptive upper bound on undetected baseline violation probability (one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound ≈ 0.00994) and provides artifact-grounded design lessons and reproducibility artifacts to guide follow-up stress tests that intentionally exercise repair (independent-generation semantics, stronger adversaries, broader verifier families, expanded repair budgets). All preregistration, per-episode validator traces, provider-call audits, and analysis artifacts required to reproduce the accounting and contingency are archived in the evidence bundle for independent verification.

limitations: Degenerate confirmatory outcome: zero discordant pairs (n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0) render McNemar inference uninformative about repair efficacy when baseline violation rates are nonzero; the preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline violation rate and targeted detecting a 30 percentage-point absolute reduction.

GVR not exercised: under the chosen task set, emulator, model, and validators the verifier never reported forbidden reachability and consequently the guarded repair step was never invoked; the experiment therefore tests whether verifier insertion changes compliance when baseline is already compliant, not whether verifier-guided repair rescues violations.

Generation contract choice: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one LLM call per pair and reduced model-call overhead but also limited independent draws that could produce discordant errors; alternative contracts (independent-condition generation or expanded repair budgets) would better exercise repair paths.

Adversarial-perturbation detail: the preregistration specified programmatic generation of one adversarial variant per benign seed; per-task generation seeds and intent payloads are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl, and the transformation logs are available in the execution manifest for reproducibility.

External validity: tasks were synthetically generated and executed in Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation; results do not necessarily generalize to heterogeneous production devices, live traffic conditions, or different operational constraints.
Model and verifier scope: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and two deterministic validators were evaluated; other LLMs, stronger verifiers, or dynamic execution oracles may produce different outcomes.

Primary confirmatory hypothesis untestable in this run: because no initial candidate triggered the forbidden-reachability predicate, the study provides no evidence that verifier-guided repair can rescue violating initial candidates; follow-up designs must intentionally produce verifier-detectable violations to evaluate repair efficacy.
